thread:
lee: Hi everyone
I just got my MBP M3 and after the initial setup the system shows 'Profile install: pending user approval' and the installer dialog asks to allow kernel extensions but the 'Allow' button is greyed out. macOS Sequoia 14.2. Any tips?

it-support: welcome lee! common cause is that the device hasn't finished the Kandji post-enroll automations. can you confirm you're on office network (redwood-employee) and not on guest? also send serial if you want extra checks.

lee: on office wifi. serial C02CD3YYYYYY. I did accept the MDM prompt but it still asks for approval in Privacy & Security.

mdm-bot: device C02CD3YYYYYY status: enrolled, policies_pending: software_policy, kernel_exts_pending: 2. Last sync: 1958002400.

sam: that means the MDM pushed a kext/driver that requires user approval. On Sequoia the flow changed: you must unlock System Settings and click Allow within 30 minutes of the install prompt. If the Allow button is greyed out, try rebooting into recovery and ensure Secure Boot setting is default (Medium).

lee: rebooted once, Allow still greyed out. any CLI workaround?

it-support: no CLI to bypass user consent for kexts. two options: 1) use our temporary admin JIT to install the entitlement via authorized app flow, 2) perform a clean reboot and open System Settings immediately after login, click 'Allow' while we trigger a re-push from Kandji. I can trigger the push now.

lee: let's do option 2. i'll reboot now and hang on Slack.

it-support: pushing kernel ext payload...

mdm-bot: push delivered at 1958002505, action: kernel_exts_redeploy.

lee: back up, opened System Settings > Privacy & Security, 'Allow' button became active when I clicked the MDM task. clicked Allow, system prompted for restart.

security: quick check: please confirm FileVault is enabled and the recovery key is escrowed in Okta before we mark this as resolved.

lee: FileVault was prompted earlier during setup; enabled. Okta shows device with serial and a recovery key entry.

it-support: great. final step: run the post-provision script to install developer tools. paste-run these commands as your local admin (we enabled temp-jit for 30m):

```
sudo /usr/local/bin/redwood_post_provision.sh
sudo /opt/homebrew/bin/brew install --cask visual-studio-code
```

lee: ran the script, VSCode installed, Docker toolbox installed fine. everything looks green. thanks all.

it-support: Root cause: delayed user-consent window + Sequoia timing. Mitigation: updated onboarding docs to advise immediate Settings check after reboot and we added an automated 're-push then notify' flow. closing unless you see more issues. :thumbsup:
